title: Building my first game.
author: kuroshikigami_
selftext:
Hey all. 

I'm planning to build an action hack'n'slash RPG. I've spent a good amount of time planning the entire thing from features to storyline to campaign, etc. 

I haven't implemented anything yet. 

My programming experience is about the level of your average programmer, I'm a doctor by profession but want to widen my expertise a bit. 

What steps do you all suggest once you've finished the backbone planning aspect of the game - the engine ideas, the hooks, etc? 

Plan is to be an isometric 3D game like a Zenonia 3/4/5 meets Diablo 2/3. 

Would appreciate any advice, it's my first time building something from scratch through vibecoding >.<

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body:
ask ai :-/ , make a game design doc , then make a slice , stripped down ugly html version using threesjs in the browser just to see it , you would also be surprised at what threejs can pull off with a frontier model and max effort. After that use ai to help build the plan and just keep at it in the engine of your choice . 

Also look around ( i have no recommendation) alot of ppl have made guides and frameworks for this sort of thing u can check them out (google / github) , remix them or make your own.

comments.author: -Star-Walker-
comments.body:
Start with a throwaway proof of concept project. A very very lite version of what you are planning. It takes some time and you will make a lot of errors. But every error you are doing in that phase (there will be a lot!!) is an error you not will not do when you start your real project. And don’t ☝️use any code from your proof of concept in your real project. DON‘T! You will regret that! Definitely 🤣  
Figure out, how to manage your assets, how to build your levels (editor?), sound, menus, controls (mobile touch, keyboard, hybrid? … important) … maybe (like what I’m planning right now) you are not doing a game, you are coding a game engine where characters, levels, etc. are just descriptions, … need a new character? No problem: create a description, throw it into your character folder … done .. playable without writing any code.

replies.author: kuroshikigami_
replies.body:
Perfect. Since I have most of the literature and concept work done, it should be easier to produce the concept project. 

Would you then tell it to make the proof of concept and once you hammer out the errors, you would make it produce a list of errors to avoid in the main project? Or is it more for checking if it would be viable?

replies.author: -Star-Walker-
replies.body:
Actually yes, I would tell my AI to log „lessons learned“ in one or several files. Better in several files „lessons-learned/character-animation.md“, „“lessons-learned/viewport-handling.md“, … so when you work on one aspect of your game, you can refer to that specific file.   
Depending on the AI you are using, you can ask it to make a skill for a task, if something went well.

comments.author: Useful_Use_6170
comments.body:
I would highly recommend a GDD nice and detailed set it in phases or pillars of your core loops design.

And start from core loop and then work your way out
